significance: A Shiva temple in the Jaunsar-Bawar hills above the Yamuna, whose surviving shikhara is dated to the 12th–13th century while brick remains on the site go back several centuries earlier. A sixth-century inscription found here records that a princess named Ishwara of Singhpura raised a shrine in memory of her husband Chandragupta, and Archaeological Survey excavations have recovered a large quantity of sculpture around it.
story: Local tradition ties the site to the Mahabharata, holding that this is where Duryodhana built the lac house in which he meant to burn the Pandavas alive.
